pr_title: Make Relax replays imported from stable work
pr_body:
Fixes #9243

Main change: Add `HandlePositionalInput` and `HandleActionInput` in `OsuFramedReplayInputHandler`
This might be a bit hacky?

Tested with some of my relax replays, and seems ok.
[Relax replays.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6252787/Relax.replays.zip)
pr_comments:
Since you didn't bother to actually *explain* what this is intending to do in the description again, I'll attempt to do it for you: as far as I can tell the intention is to make the relax mod always handle pressed actions instead of attempting to read them from the replay, as apparently stable replay frames don't contain information when the key was automatically pressed. So `HandlePositionalInput` is not really needed in this pull, and was added mostly for symmetry, I suppose.

This means that any replay will now always use the exact relax implementation at the time of playback. As a result, there is no guarantee that all legacy relax replays will play back 100% correctly (as I understand the auto-click algorithm is a bit different in lazer), but that's a bit of a lost cause unless the algorithm is replicated perfectly. It also means that if the implementation changes in the future, past replays may break even if they have the clicks registered in the replay. I don't know if that last part is fine. It may be for now.

>It also means that if the implementation changes in the future, past replays may break even if they have the clicks registered in the replay.

Correct.
In stable, since it doesn't record action frames, it will also change the playback if the relax mod logic has changed, I belive this behavior is intended because relax SHOULD be generating clicks on playback instead of when playing
Breaking past replays is generally a no-no. Historical plays should be preserved as they were, if possible.

> Breaking past replays is generally a no-no.

I didn't change the logic of relax mod, so unless there are any changes in the future, replays made before this shouldn't be affected (I suppose?), since they're generating clicks with the same logic.

Or add a check if there's recorded action frames present and use them. But I think this will need to expose more methods, as there are no way to access replay data from a mod right?

> But I think this will need to expose more methods, as there are no way to access replay data from a mod right?

The way I'd do that is make a separate relax-specific subclass of `OsuFramedReplayInputHandler` that can be used to inspect the replay and decide whether or not clicks should be simulated by the mod. I'd like to see the others' thoughts on this direction first, though.

> > But I think this will need to expose more methods, as there are no way to access replay data from a mod right?
> 
> The way I'd do that is make a separate relax-specific subclass of `OsuFramedReplayInputHandler` that can be used to inspect the replay and decide whether or not clicks should be simulated by the mod. I'd like to see the others' thoughts on this direction first, though.

My thought was to add a public method of `getReplayLoaded()` in `OsuFramedReplayInputHandler`
Another issue is that `relax_leniency` mismatch(less than) from stable, and I noticed this causing replays having more miss than stable. But that's another PR maybe
Definitely not in scope here.

Haven't looked into this in detail (and probably won't for a long time since it's such an edge case / unimportant issue), but heads up that I'm not sure this is the correct direction. It potentially introduces actual inaccuracy in newly made replays, as the time of clicks may be calculated using local frames rather than replay playback frames.

May make more sense to handle this at legacy replay import time.

There are a lot of context only during gameplay is lost, and there's no rulset-specific score decoders(I'm only handling osu! ruleset relax replays)

It may not match 100% due to different relax mod implementation, but how about checking the incoming replay data for *any* reported actions, and if there are none present, allowing the mod to run its input handling (`Update`) code?

issue_context.title: Relax replays imported from stable doesn't play properly
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:**
Relax replays imported from stable doesn't play correctly in lazer. The cursor movement is correct, but it shows every note as a miss (even if the cursor is on the right place at the right time).
Relax replayer generated "natively" in lazer doesn't suffer from this issue.

How to reproduce:
1) Make sure you have relax scores in stable. If not, play a map with relax, press F2 to save replay at result screen, and double-click the .osr file to import that replay
2) Launch osu!lazer, choose settings->import scores from stable
3) watch the replay of imported relax scores

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:**
![图片](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66686071/84164868-9dae6800-aaa5-11ea-822d-4a0475a65356.png)

**osu!lazer version:** 
2020.603.0

**Logs:**

[performance.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/4752990/performance.log)
[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/4752991/runtime.log)
[updater.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/4752992/updater.log)
[database.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/4752993/database.log)
[network.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/4752997/network.log)

review_comments:
This will cause lazer-made classic scores to use input from this mod instead of the replay frames.

How about instead clearing the actions of all replay frames at decode time if made with stable? There's already this condition to determine if an incoming score was made on stable:
https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/52b9616909d57f514dcca68c8e21ac4e1de138c0/osu.Game/Scoring/Legacy/LegacyScoreDecoder.cs#L69

Then, this mod could check if `score.Replay.Frames.Any(f => (f as OsuReplayFrame)?.Actions.Any() == true);`

Edit: On second thought it might just be the same thing for the case where a lazer-made classic score has 0 frames... May be fine as is...

Still not sure on this one.

Maybe cc @peppy - tl;dr: there's no way to currently know if a replay is a stable-made replay from within the relax mod, and this PR is using `ModClassic` being present as the heuristic instead.

From discussions above, my suggestion was to detect stable replays at decode time and clear all actions, then switch on that in this code instead (indicating all frames with 0 actions == stable-made replay == relax mod does the hits even in replays).  
However that has the potential that, suppose, if a lazer-made classic-mod replay exists with 0 actions and the relax mod changes its leniency or whatever, it'll also perform the hits in the lazer-made replay.

I'm not sure there's a better way other than one of the two methods proposed - the existing code in this PR, or my own proposal.

Is another potential solution to wait until we expand `ScoreInfo` to contain some kind of version specification, where we can determine whether a score was set on stable or lazer (regardless of `ModClassic`)? I don't see this issue as a super-high priority one, so it might be better to wait for such a solution if it sounds amicable.
Yeah that was another thought going in my head, but I wasn't seeing the bigger picture. Shall we close this for the time being then?
I'd say so. Not against temporary fixes but this one is really hard to warrant..
